calls.head: Good looks against hopeful ones
calls.body: On shot quality, Montréal is the league’s best and Nashville is near the bottom of the league. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Canadiens’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Predators’.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On how dangerous the average shot was, Montréal had 7.1% a shot and Nashville 3.8% a shot. Coming in, Montréal was at 6.9% a shot and Nashville at 6.1% a shot.
calls.usual: MTL 6.9% a shot · NSH 6.1% a shot
calls.tonight: MTL 7.1% a shot · NSH 3.8% a shot
calls.beyond: Nashville’s shots at 5-on-5 were less dangerous than usual: a 3.8% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.1% (league average 6.3%). A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

calls.head: The Canadiens hit; the Predators mostly don’t
calls.body: On physicality, Montréal is near the top of the league and Nashville is one of the league’s worst. That’s about as far apart as two teams get.
calls.call: The Canadiens hit more than the Predators in the close stretches of the game.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On hit score in close games (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average), Montréal had hit score 52 and Nashville hit score 78. Coming in, Montréal was at hit score 109 and Nashville at hit score 85.
calls.usual: MTL hit score 109 · NSH hit score 85
calls.tonight: MTL hit score 52 · NSH hit score 78

MTL.head: We had this close to even (55% for Montréal), and it went Nashville’s way.

NSH.head: We had this close to even (45% for Nashville), and Nashville came through.

surprises.head: Nashville won against the run of play
surprises.body: Played out 100 times with these chances, Montréal wins 77. Nashville won anyway.

surprises.head: Montréal hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Montréal’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 52, against their usual 109 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 45 games.
surprises.flipped: The Canadiens hit; the Predators mostly don’t

story.head: The Predators come back from two down
paras: Nick Suzuki opened the scoring early in the second. Adam Edstrom added two goals. Four different Predators scored. The Canadiens led by two, but the Predators came all the way back.

The score flatters the Predators: the Canadiens had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Canadiens win about four in five. Juuse Saros made the difference in net, stopping 31 of 33.

items.text: The Canadiens haven’t won in three.
One of the preview’s two calls held.
